cases.question: Which units are vacant right now?
cases.title: Vacant units right now
cases.sql:
SELECT b.name AS building, u.unit_number AS unit, u.unit_type AS type, u.bedrooms AS bedrooms, u.sqft AS sqft, u.monthly_rent AS monthly_rent
FROM unit u
JOIN building b ON b.building_id = u.building_id
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM lease l JOIN lease_status s ON s.status_id = l.status_id
  WHERE l.unit_id = u.unit_id AND s.is_current = 1
)
ORDER BY b.name, u.unit_number
assumptions: A unit is vacant when it has no current lease; current leases are Active - Fixed Term, Active - Month to Month and Notice Given.
Units with only ended, evicted or pending-signature leases (or no lease) count as vacant.
Units with Notice Given leases are treated as still occupied.

Check: The query decides occupancy only from the lease status flag and never checks lease start or end dates, so a lease that has already expired but is still marked Active would hide a unit that is really vacant. Check that the active leases shown are actually in force today.

cases.question: List tenants who currently have a lease, with their unit and monthly rent.
cases.title: Tenants with a current lease, their unit and monthly rent
cases.sql:
SELECT t.first_name || ' ' || t.last_name AS "Tenant", b.name AS "Building", u.unit_number AS "Unit", ls.label AS "Lease status", u.monthly_rent AS "Monthly rent"
FROM lease l
JOIN lease_status ls ON ls.status_id = l.status_id
JOIN tenant t ON t.tenant_id = l.tenant_id
JOIN unit u ON u.unit_id = l.unit_id
JOIN building b ON b.building_id = u.building_id
WHERE ls.is_current = 1
ORDER BY t.last_name, t.first_name
assumptions: 'Currently has a lease' means the lease status is marked as current: Active - Fixed Term, Active - Month to Month, or Notice Given.
Pending Signature, Ended and Evicted leases are excluded.
Monthly rent is the listed rent of the unit.
A tenant appears once per current lease.

Check: The "Monthly rent" column comes from the unit's listed rent, not from the rent on each tenant's lease, so check that the lease itself does not carry a different agreed rent before showing these figures as what each tenant pays.

cases.question: How many maintenance requests are still open in each building?
cases.title: Open maintenance requests by building
cases.sql: SELECT b.name AS building, COUNT(m.request_id) AS open_requests FROM building b JOIN unit u ON u.building_id=b.building_id LEFT JOIN maintenance m ON m.unit_id=u.unit_id AND m.state<>'closed' GROUP BY b.building_id, b.name ORDER BY open_requests DESC
assumptions: 'Still open' means any request that is not closed yet: open, in progress, or waiting for parts.
Buildings with no unresolved requests are still listed with a count of 0.
Requests are assigned to buildings through the unit they were raised for.

cases.question: Which tenants paid rent late at least once in 2026?

questions.question: What counts as a late rent payment?
options: Paid any day after the due date (1+ days)
Paid more than 5 days after the due date (typical grace period; payments are mostly 1–2 days late or earlier, with a separate cluster at 6+ days)
Paid after the due date, or still unpaid when the due date has passed

cases.question: Total rent collected per region in 2026.
cases.title: Rent collected per region in 2026
cases.sql:
SELECT r.name AS region, ROUND(SUM(p.amount), 2) AS total_rent_collected, COUNT(*) AS payments_received
FROM payment p
JOIN lease l ON l.lease_id = p.lease_id
JOIN unit u ON u.unit_id = l.unit_id
JOIN building b ON b.building_id = u.building_id
JOIN region r ON r.region_id = b.region_id
WHERE p.paid_on IS NOT NULL AND p.paid_on >= '2026-01-01' AND p.paid_on < '2027-01-01'
GROUP BY r.name
ORDER BY total_rent_collected DESC
assumptions: Rent collected means payments that have actually been received (they have a paid date); unpaid dues are excluded.
2026 is based on the date the payment was received, from 1 Jan 2026 through today's data.
Each payment is assigned to a region through its lease's unit and building.
All payment methods and all lease statuses are included.

cases.question: Urgent maintenance requests that are not closed, with the technician assigned.
cases.title: Open urgent maintenance requests with assigned technician
cases.sql:
SELECT m.request_id AS "Request", m.unit_id AS "Unit", m.category AS "Category", m.opened AS "Opened", m.state AS "Status", COALESCE(s.first_name || ' ' || s.last_name, 'Unassigned') AS "Technician"
FROM maintenance m
LEFT JOIN staff s ON s.staff_id = m.assigned_to
WHERE m.priority = 'urgent' AND m.state <> 'closed'
ORDER BY m.opened
assumptions: 'Not closed' means the request status is open, in progress or waiting for parts.
Requests with no technician assigned are still listed and shown as 'Unassigned'.
Sorted by oldest opened date first.

Check: The filter excludes only 'closed', but the stated assumption defines 'not closed' as open, in progress or waiting for parts, so check whether any other status values (such as cancelled or on hold) exist and should be left out.

cases.question: Average number of days to close a plumbing request.
cases.title: Average days to close a plumbing request
cases.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS closed_plumbing_requests, ROUND(AVG(julianday(closed) - julianday(opened)), 1) AS avg_days_to_close FROM maintenance WHERE category = 'plumbing' AND state = 'closed' AND closed IS NOT NULL
assumptions: Only plumbing requests that are already closed are included; open, in-progress and waiting-for-parts requests are excluded.
Days to close = calendar days from the opened date to the closed date.
All time, no date filter applied.

cases.question: Leases ending between 2026-10-01 and 2026-12-31.
cases.title: Leases ending between 1 Oct and 31 Dec 2026
cases.sql: SELECT l.lease_id AS "Lease", t.first_name || ' ' || t.last_name AS "Tenant", b.name AS "Building", u.unit_number AS "Unit", s.label AS "Lease status", l.start_date AS "Start date", l.end_date AS "End date", u.monthly_rent AS "Monthly rent" FROM lease l JOIN tenant t ON t.tenant_id = l.tenant_id JOIN unit u ON u.unit_id = l.unit_id JOIN building b ON b.building_id = u.building_id JOIN lease_status s ON s.status_id = l.status_id WHERE l.end_date BETWEEN '2026-10-01' AND '2026-12-31' ORDER BY l.end_date
assumptions: Leases are matched on their scheduled end date, with both 1 Oct 2026 and 31 Dec 2026 included.
Leases with no end date (open-ended) are not included.
All lease statuses are included, with the status shown so you can filter.

Check: The "Monthly rent" column comes from the unit's rent rather than the lease's own agreed rent, so it may not match what each tenant actually pays under that lease. Check it against the lease record before relying on it.

cases.question: Which buildings have an elevator and more than 10 units?
cases.title: Buildings with an elevator and more than 10 units
cases.sql: SELECT b.name AS building, b.street AS street, b.city AS city, COUNT(u.unit_id) AS unit_count FROM building b JOIN unit u ON u.building_id = b.building_id WHERE b.has_elevator = 1 GROUP BY b.building_id, b.name, b.street, b.city HAVING COUNT(u.unit_id) > 10 ORDER BY unit_count DESC
assumptions: Has an elevator means the building is flagged as having an elevator.
More than 10 units means 11 or more units recorded for the building, regardless of whether they are leased or vacant.

cases.question: Evicted tenants and their email addresses.
cases.title: Evicted tenants and their email addresses
cases.sql:
SELECT t.first_name AS "First name", t.last_name AS "Last name", t.email AS "Email"
FROM tenant t
JOIN lease l ON l.tenant_id = t.tenant_id
JOIN lease_status s ON s.status_id = l.status_id
WHERE s.label = 'Evicted'
ORDER BY t.last_name, t.first_name
assumptions: Evicted tenants are those whose lease has the status 'Evicted'.
Each tenant has one lease, so each appears once.
